parts.title: Olvasott szöveg értése
parts.name: The rise of the repair café
parts.text:
In a community hall in Bristol, a retired engineer is examining a broken toaster while its owner watches nervously. Ten minutes later, the toaster is working again, and the owner has learned how to replace a fuse. This is a repair café, one of more than two thousand that now operate around the world.

The idea began in Amsterdam in 2009, when a journalist called Martine Postma decided that throwing away broken objects had become far too normal. She organised a single event where volunteers with practical skills offered to fix things for free. The response was so enthusiastic that she soon set up a foundation to help other communities copy the model.

Supporters say repair cafés do much more than reduce waste. Visitors often arrive feeling frustrated with products that seem designed to fail, but leave feeling more confident about understanding the objects they own. "People are surprised by how simple many repairs are," says one volunteer. "Often it's just a loose wire."

There are limits, however. Many modern devices are glued together or need special tools, and manufacturers do not always make spare parts available. Campaigners argue that new laws are needed to give consumers a genuine "right to repair". Several countries have recently introduced rules forcing companies to supply parts and repair manuals for a number of years.

For now, the cafés rely on volunteers, donated tools and a great deal of goodwill. But as one regular visitor puts it, "You don't just fix your kettle here. You meet your neighbours."

lines.hu: Tom, a múlt hétvégét egy vadvédelmi központban töltötted önkéntesként. Hogy jött ez?

lines.hu: A nővérem ott dolgozik, és kevesen voltak, így rábeszélt, hogy segítsek.

lines.hu: Mit kellett ténylegesen csinálnod?

lines.it: Mostly cleaning, to be honest. But on Sunday I helped feed two young foxes, which was amazing.
lines.hu: Őszintén szólva főleg takarítani. De vasárnap segítettem megetetni két fiatal rókát, ami csodálatos volt.

lines.it: Would you do it again?

parts.title: Olvasott szöveg értése
parts.name: The myth of multitasking
parts.text:
Few skills are more widely admired in the modern workplace than the ability to multitask. Job advertisements routinely request it, and many of us take quiet pride in answering emails during meetings or drafting reports while monitoring a stream of messages. Yet a growing body of research suggests that what we call multitasking is, in most cases, something rather less impressive.

Neuroscientists point out that the brain does not genuinely perform two demanding tasks at once. Instead, it switches rapidly between them, and each switch carries a cost. Attention must be withdrawn from one task and re-engaged with another, and in the process small amounts of time and accuracy are lost. Over a working day, these losses accumulate into what some researchers estimate to be a reduction in productivity of up to forty per cent.

Perhaps more troubling is the finding that habitual multitaskers tend to overestimate their own abilities. In laboratory studies, those who reported multitasking most frequently often performed worse at filtering out irrelevant information than those who rarely did so. The very habit that people believe sharpens their minds may, paradoxically, be dulling them.

None of this means that all combinations of activity are equally harmful. Listening to music while running, or chatting while cooking a familiar dish, places little strain on our cognitive resources, because one of the activities has become largely automatic. The difficulty arises when both tasks require conscious thought.

Some organisations have begun to respond. A number of firms now encourage "focus hours" during which notifications are switched off and meetings are banned. Early reports are cautiously positive, though critics note that such schemes depend heavily on managers modelling the behaviour themselves. A policy announced by email and then ignored by senior staff is unlikely to change anything.

questions.q: What is the writer's main point in the first paragraph?
o: A widely valued skill may be misunderstood.
Job adverts are becoming more demanding.
Meetings are a waste of time.

questions.why: A szokás, ami állítólag élesíti az elmét, valójában tompítja.

questions.q: What condition do critics mention for focus hours to succeed?
o: Managers must follow the rules themselves.
questions.why: "depend heavily on managers modelling the behaviour"

lines.it: Dr Hughes, your research focuses on urban noise. Why should we care about it?
lines.hu: Dr. Hughes, a kutatása a városi zajra összpontosít. Miért kellene ezzel foglalkoznunk?

lines.it: Because it's one of the most underestimated health risks we face. Chronic noise raises stress levels and disrupts sleep, even when people believe they've got used to it.
lines.hu: Mert ez az egyik leginkább alábecsült egészségügyi kockázat. A tartós zaj növeli a stresszt és rontja az alvást, még akkor is, ha az emberek azt hiszik, hozzászoktak.

lines.it: So the idea that we simply adapt is a myth?
lines.hu: Tehát az, hogy egyszerűen alkalmazkodunk, mítosz?

lines.it: Largely, yes. People may stop noticing it consciously, but their bodies continue to react.
lines.hu: Nagyrészt igen. Az emberek tudatosan talán már nem veszik észre, de a testük továbbra is reagál.

lines.it: What are cities doing about it?
lines.hu: Mit tesznek ellene a városok?

lines.it: Some are reducing speed limits, which lowers tyre noise considerably. Others are planting trees, although their effect on noise is smaller than people assume.
lines.hu: Néhányan csökkentik a sebességhatárokat, ami jelentősen mérsékli a gumik zaját. Mások fákat ültetnek, bár ezek hatása a zajra kisebb, mint gondolnák.

lines.it: Interesting. So trees are mainly symbolic?
lines.hu: Érdekes. Tehát a fák inkább szimbolikusak?

lines.it: Not entirely. They make streets feel calmer, and that perception matters for well-being, even if the decibels barely change.
lines.hu: Nem teljesen. Nyugodtabbnak érződnek tőlük az utcák, és ez az érzet számít a jólléthez, még ha a decibelek alig változnak is.

lines.it: And what can individuals do?
lines.hu: És mit tehetnek az egyének?

lines.it: Protect their sleep above all. A quiet bedroom is probably the single most effective change most people can make.
lines.hu: Mindenekelőtt óvják az alvásukat. Egy csendes hálószoba valószínűleg a leghatékonyabb változtatás, amit a legtöbben megtehetnek.

o: The body still reacts to it.

questions.q: Which measure reduces noise considerably?

o: Their effect on noise is smaller than expected.
